title: Girls' Hair for Functions: Styles That Survive
meta_description: Hairstyles for girls that last a whole wedding or Eid day, which accessories stay put, and how to work with the hair she actually has.
keywords: girls hairstyles for functions, kids hair accessories Pakistan, wedding hairstyle for child, Eid hairstyle girls, hair styles that last all day
excerpt: The hairstyle is done at six and gone by eight. Here is what actually survives a function, and which accessories stay in.
imagePrompt: A flat-lay of children's hair accessories on cream linen — a row of satin-covered hair bands in ivory, sage and dusty rose, small pearl-tipped pins, fabric-covered snap clips, a soft bristle brush and two silk scrunchies. A folded child's dupatta in soft focus behind. Bright natural daylight, shallow depth of field, delicate editorial flat-lay in warm neutrals, no faces, no text.

content.content:
The hair is done carefully at six o'clock. By eight it has half fallen out, the clip is somewhere on a floor, and the elaborate style is a ponytail put in by a cousin.

This happens because children's function hair is usually styled the way an adult's is — for a photograph — when it needs to be styled for four hours of running, dancing, sitting on floors and being picked up.

Those are different problems with different answers. A style that survives is not a less pretty style; it is a style built to hold, on the hair she actually has, with accessories that cannot work loose.

Here is what works, roughly in order of how long it lasts.

content.heading: Styles That Genuinely Last
content.content:
**A braided crown or halo braid.** The most durable style there is. Everything is contained, nothing hangs loose, and it looks finished for hours. It takes longer to do and it is worth it.

**Two French or Dutch braids.** Secure, comfortable, and they hold through anything. They also come out as soft waves the next day, which is a bonus.

**A low bun with the front sections braided back.** Formal enough for a wedding, and the braids stop the front escaping — which is where every style fails first.

**A half-up style with the top section braided.** Good for hair that is too fine to hold a full updo.

**A high ponytail with the base wrapped in a section of hair.** Simple, and looks considerably more finished than a plain ponytail.

**What does not last:** loose curls, anything relying on hairspray, half-up styles with a single clip, and elaborate updos with many pinned sections. Curls in most Pakistani hair drop within two hours in humidity, and a style with fifteen pins loses them one at a time.

content.heading: Working With the Hair She Has
content.content:
**Fine, straight hair** does not hold a bun or a pin. Braids are the answer, because they hold mechanically rather than by grip. Texturising spray or a light plait-before-styling helps. Avoid heavy accessories, which slide straight out.

**Thick, coarse hair** holds almost anything but needs more securing than you expect — the weight works against you. Use more elastics than seems necessary and secure in sections.

**Curly hair** should generally not be brushed out for a function. Work with the curl: a half-up style, a pinned-back front, or a loose braid. Fighting the texture takes an hour and lasts twenty minutes.

**Short hair** takes a headband, small clips at the sides, or a partial braid at the front. Do not attempt a bun.

**Very long hair** benefits from being contained rather than displayed. A single long braid or a low bun is more comfortable for her and more practical at a function than loose hair, which gets caught in everything.

**Oiled hair** — common before a function in many households — will not hold a style at all. Wash it the night before, not the morning of.

content.heading: Accessories That Stay In
content.content:
The main criterion is mechanical grip, not appearance.

**Fabric-covered snap clips** hold better than metal ones and do not pull. The most reliable accessory for fine hair.

**Satin or fabric-covered hair bands** stay put, do not slip and do not press behind the ears the way a hard plastic one does. Our [hair bands](/accessories/hair-bands) section covers these.

**Small pearl-tipped or decorative pins** work well pushed into a braid, where the braid itself holds them. Pushed into loose hair they fall out.

**Silk scrunchies** are gentler than elastics and hold thick hair well.

**Small flowers pinned into a braid** are the prettiest option that actually lasts, because the braid does the holding. Our [hair clips](/accessories/hair-clips) section has pieces that work this way.

**What falls out:** large decorative clips on fine hair, hard plastic headbands, anything heavy, and elaborate hair chains on a young child.

**Two of everything.** Whatever she wears, bring a spare. Something will be lost, and a matching pair with one missing is worse than either.

content.heading: Comfort, Which Decides Everything
content.content:
A style she is uncomfortable in will be undone by her within an hour, and she will be right to undo it.

**Not too tight.** A tight braid or ponytail pulls at the scalp and causes a headache within an hour. She will not always say so — she will just pull at it. Tight enough to hold, no tighter.

**Nothing pressing behind the ears.** Hard headbands are the usual offender.

**Nothing sharp against the scalp.** Check pin ends and clip teeth with your fingers before they go in.

**Nothing hanging that she can pull.** A hanging decorative chain will be pulled, by her or by another child.

**Consider the dupatta.** If she is wearing one, a high bun and a dupatta over the head do not combine — the bun pushes the dupatta forward all evening. A low bun or braids sit flat underneath.

**Do it early enough to test.** An hour before leaving, not five minutes. If she is going to complain, you want to know while there is still time to change it.

content.heading: Timing and Preparation
content.content:
**Wash the night before, not the morning of.** Freshly washed hair is slippery and holds a style badly. A day-old wash holds considerably better.

**Do not oil before a function.** Oiled hair will not hold anything. Oil after, not before.

**Detangle properly first**, from the ends upward. Rushing this is where the crying happens, and a distressed child before a function sets the tone for the evening.

**Damp, not wet.** Slightly damp hair braids more neatly and sets better. Soaking wet hair takes hours to dry inside a braid and can smell.

**Allow twice the time you think.** Children move, and a rushed style is a loose style.

**Style before the outfit goes on**, so nothing is pulled over her head afterwards.

**Take a photograph when it is done.** If it needs redoing at the function by someone else, a picture makes that possible.

content.heading: Matching the Style to the Occasion
content.content:
**Mehndi and dholki.** Braids, flowers, and colour. She will be dancing, so secure everything. Fresh flowers pinned into a braid suit the occasion and cost almost nothing. Our [dholki guide](/journal/how-to-dress-kids-pakistani-dholki-night) covers the setting.

**Barat and walima.** More formal — a low bun, a braided crown, or a half-up style with pearl pins. This is where the good accessories belong. Our [kids' festive wear guide](/journal/kids-festive-wear-guide-pakistani-weddings) maps the functions.

**Nikah.** Simple and neat, and flat enough to sit under a dupatta if she is covering her head.

**Eid morning.** Whatever she wants, within reason. It is her day and there is no dress code beyond neat.

**School functions.** Secure and simple, and check whether the school specifies anything. Our [school function guide](/journal/kids-school-function-annual-day-outfits) covers the wider question, and a style that survives a rehearsal and a performance needs to be a braid.

**Winter functions.** Anything that survives a shawl or a hood being pulled on and off repeatedly, which rules out most updos.

content.heading: Repairing It at the Function
content.content:
Something will come loose. Being able to fix it in two minutes is the difference between a small moment and a sulk that lasts an hour.

**Carry a small pouch:** a brush or comb, four spare elastics, six spare pins, two spare clips, and a small mirror.

**Learn one emergency style** you can do in ninety seconds without good light — usually a low ponytail with the front twisted back and pinned. It looks deliberate and takes no skill.

**Do not attempt a full re-style at a function.** Contain what has come loose and move on.

**Let her have a say.** By six or seven she has opinions, and a style she chose is one she leaves alone. A slightly less perfect style she likes lasts far longer than a perfect one she does not.

**Take the photographs early.** Hair looks best in the first hour, and the group photographs at Pakistani functions often happen late. Get your own pictures at the start.

The [hair bands](/accessories/hair-bands) and [hair clips](/accessories/hair-clips) sections have spares worth keeping in the bag, and the wider [accessories collection](/accessories) has hand-crafted pieces for the more formal functions.

questions.question: What hairstyle lasts longest on a child at a function?
questions.answer: A braided crown or two French braids. Braids hold mechanically rather than by grip, so nothing works loose over four hours of running and dancing. A low bun with the front sections braided back is the most formal option that still survives the evening.

questions.question: Which hair accessories actually stay in?
questions.answer: Fabric-covered snap clips, satin-covered hair bands, silk scrunchies, and small pins pushed into a braid where the braid holds them. Large decorative clips on fine hair, hard plastic headbands and anything heavy all fall out. Bring a spare of whatever she wears.

questions.question: Should I wash my daughter's hair before a function?
questions.answer: The night before, not the morning of. Freshly washed hair is slippery and holds a style badly, while a day-old wash holds considerably better. Do not oil beforehand — oiled hair will not hold anything at all.

questions.question: How do I style hair that will be under a dupatta?
questions.answer: Flat and low. A high bun pushes a dupatta forward all evening and she will spend the function adjusting it. A low bun, braids or a braided crown sit flat underneath and stay comfortable.

questions.question: What should I carry to fix her hair at a function?
questions.answer: A comb, four spare elastics, six pins, two clips and a small mirror in a pouch. Learn one emergency style you can do in ninety seconds — a low ponytail with the front twisted back and pinned works and looks deliberate. Do not attempt a full restyle mid-function.
